html:
A rising of Albanian settlers and Greek landholders in the Byzantine Despotate of the Morea, in the southern Peloponnese, in 1453 and 1454.

After the fall of Constantinople the Morea was the last sizeable Byzantine land, split between two quarrelling brothers of Constantine XI, the despots Thomas and Demetrios Palaiologos. Many Albanians had settled there as farmers and soldiers. They rose against the despots, chose leaders of their own, including a Greek noble of the Kantakouzenos family, and besieged the despots in their towns.

With no one else to turn to, the brothers asked the Ottomans for help. An Ottoman army crushed the revolt in 1454, and in return the despots paid tribute to Mehmed II. They kept quarrelling and fell behind on payments, which gave Mehmed his reason to conquer the Morea in 1460.
sum: A rising of Albanian settlers and Greek landholders in the Byzantine Despotate of the Morea, in the southern Peloponnese, in 1453 and 1454.
